name: Kim Min-jun
action: Kim Min-jun rocks the carrier slowly as Seo-yeon’s breathing evens out, then rubs his eyes with one hand. He reopens his calendar and spreadsheet, confirming the vaccination date and the emailed test dates side by side. Satisfied, he opens the reply window and types, deletes, retypes, pauses, then sends a short message: 'Thank you for the invitation. The second day of the on-site test conflicts with a personal commitment I cannot move. Would it be possible to shift both days by one day, or move only the second day to the following Monday? I am happy to work around your schedule; the originally proposed dates are otherwise flexible for me. Best regards, Kim Min-jun.' He closes the laptop, glances at the red circle on the wall calendar, and lets out a slow breath.
reason: Min-jun recognized the company as the one whose extended parental leave and flexible hours he had circled on its benefits page three weeks ago and regarded as a verifiable asset. The second test date colliding with Seo-yeon’s vaccination triggered his determination that her schedule matter more than work, shaped by his father having missed his appointments and by his own previous decision to cancel an assessment when Seo-yeon was sick. Seeing that his wife was on a double shift that day and unwilling to make her scramble, he felt his mother-in-law was the last resort because she needed notice and had sighed when swapping shifts before. He also remembered that raising parental leave early in a prior process had made the conversation stop, so he deliberately avoided mentioning Seo-yeon to the recruiter. Exhausted from Seo-yeon’s teething, he framed the issue as a scheduling problem he could solve and asked the recruiter for a one-day shift framed as a personal commitment, offering flexibility in return while reasoning that if the company genuinely valued flexibility they would accommodate him, and if not he did not want the job anyway.
